span.p:
SC-003 exception
A claims manager is answering questions about section 7. They have strong views about how it should be built.

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Trigger
They say "it should push the decision to the adjuster's phone".

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They are asked what the adjuster gets from that

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They say the adjuster is in the field and cannot wait until they are back at a desk

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see a requirement recorded as the adjuster being able to act on the claim away from their desk, with criteria about what they can do and see

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see that "push to the phone" was kept on a list of candidate architecture decisions, to hand to the engineering lead

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: No argument is had about whether a notification is the right design

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Expected
The requirement names no technology, the user need is recorded, the expert's preference is preserved for the architecture discussion, and the expert does not feel overruled.
